chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

A man said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'We find an aroma in the food of a wedding feast that is not found elsewhere.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'There is no wedding in which a camel is sacrificed, or a cow is slaughtered, or a sheep, except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sends an angel with it carrying a carat of musk from Paradise until it blends into their food. That is the aroma which is smelled because of that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the source of the pleasant aroma in wedding feast food according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical reality behind the distinct fragrance of wedding feasts, linking it to the sacrifice of an animal. He explains that upon slaughter, Allah dispatches an angel carrying a 'qirat' (a specific measure) of Paradise's musk to infuse the food, thereby elevating the sensory experience of the guests as a divine blessing. This highlights the Shia view of mundane acts of gratitude and celebration as opportunities for spiritual and physical enhancement through celestial intervention.
